thread.title: Harrigan introduces SAFE Drivers Act to standardize English testing for commercial drivers
thread.title_full: Harrigan introduces SAFE Drivers Act to standardize English testing for commercial drivers

author: t. g. unger
title: Harrigan introduces SAFE Drivers Act to standardize English testing for commercial drivers
text:
Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) has introduced the Standardized Assessment for Fluency in English for Drivers Act (SAFE Drivers Act) in the House of Representatives. The bill, co-sponsored by Rep. Troy Nehls (TX-22) and Rep. Bob Onder (MO-03), aims to create a uniform English proficiency test for all commercial driver’s license (CDL) applicants across the United States.
“If you can’t read ‘Bridge Out Ahead’ or communicate with a state trooper at a crash scene, you have no business driving an 80,000-pound truck on American highways,” said Congressman Harrigan. “We have federal rules that require English proficiency, but no standardized test to enforce them, so states like California hand out commercial licenses to drivers who can’t understand basic safety instructions. The SAFE Drivers Act fixes that by requiring one uniform English test nationwide before any CDL is issued. No more guesswork, no more state-by-state loopholes, just one standard that keeps Americans safe.”
Currently, federal law requires commercial drivers to demonstrate basic English skills, but there is no single national test to ensure compliance. States interpret and apply the rule differently, leading to inconsistent enforcement and potential safety risks. The SAFE Drivers Act directs the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) to develop and implement a standard English proficiency test to be used during both the issuance and renewal of CDLs in every state. The exam would cover reading road signs, understanding spoken instructions, and completing written reports. States that do not comply risk losing federal highway funding.
The proposed legislation has received support from the trucking industry. Congressman Harrigan is calling on fellow lawmakers to back the bill and address enforcement gaps that he says endanger lives on American roads.
In 2024, Pat Harrigan won the general election against Ralph R. Scott, Jr., receiving 57.5% of the vote.
